Most of my publications can be found at [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=VcrhCsgAAAAJ&hl=en). Below, work in progress is listed first; let me know if you want more information about any of these projects.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(RefManageR)

suppressWarnings(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))

# Helper: extract a field value (raw string) from a BibEntry
field <- function(entry, f) {
  e <- unclass(entry)[[1]]
  v <- e[[f]]
  if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0 || (length(v) == 1 && is.na(v))) return("")
  if (inherits(v, "person")) return(format(v))
  as.character(v)
}

# --- Google Scholar cross-reference -----------------------------------------
#
# We only want to show a "find on Google Scholar" icon for entries that are
# actually listed on Ingmar's Scholar profile (rather than guessing via a
# generic title search for every single entry). Scholar itself can't be
# queried at render time (it blocks non-browser requests), so instead we keep
# a local snapshot of the profile's publication titles -- data/scholar-titles.txt,
# one title per line, scraped from
# https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=VcrhCsgAAAAJ&hl=en&cstart=0&pagesize=100
# (click "Show more" to load all, then collect `.gsc_a_at` link text).
# Refresh that file occasionally to pick up newly indexed papers.
norm_title <- function(s) {
  s <- tolower(s)
  s <- iconv(s, from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")
  s <- gsub("[^a-z0-9 ]", " ", s)
  s <- gsub("\\s+", " ", s)
  trimws(s)
}

.scholar_titles_path <- "data/scholar-titles.txt"
scholar_titles_norm <- if (file.exists(.scholar_titles_path)) {
  vapply(readLines(.scholar_titles_path, warn = FALSE), norm_title, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
} else character(0)

# Is `title` (already brace-stripped) listed on the Scholar profile? Mirrors
# the matching rules used to build the snapshot: exact match, containment
# (only when the shorter/contained string is itself long & specific, >= 30
# normalized characters -- short generic titles like "Hidden Markov Models"
# are substrings of many unrelated titles and would otherwise false-match),
# or a shared, sufficiently long prefix (handles subtitle truncation).
on_scholar <- function(title) {
  bn <- norm_title(title)
  if (nchar(bn) < 3 || length(scholar_titles_norm) == 0) return(FALSE)
  any(vapply(scholar_titles_norm, function(sn) {
    min_len <- min(nchar(sn), nchar(bn))
    if (sn == bn) return(TRUE)
    if (min_len >= 30 && (grepl(sn, bn, fixed = TRUE) || grepl(bn, sn, fixed = TRUE))) return(TRUE)
    if (nchar(bn) >= 35 && nchar(sn) >= 35 && substr(sn, 1, 35) == substr(bn, 1, 35)) return(TRUE)
    FALSE
  }, logical(1)))
}

# Build a small row of icon links (DOI, OSF, GitHub, Google Scholar) for an entry,
# using academicons (ai-*) for scholarly icons and bootstrap-icons (bi-*, already
# bundled with Quarto) for GitHub/generic links.
icon_link <- function(href, icon_class, label) {
  sprintf(
    '<a class="ref-icon" href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener" aria-label="%s" title="%s"><i class="%s"></i></a>',
    href, label, label, icon_class
  )
}

# --- Status and document fields ----------------------------------------------
#
# ingmar.bib (maintained in the ingmarbib repo) uses two custom fields:
#   status   = pipeline stage of a not-yet-published project, e.g. "in preparation",
#              "under review", "in revision", "IPA", "in press". Published papers
#              have no status.
#   document = what kind of document the entry currently is, optionally with a
#              link; multi-valued, separated by semicolons, e.g.
#              "preprint", "stage 1 registered report", "preregistration",
#              "preprint: https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/xxxxx".
# plus `osf` (OSF project: materials, data, ...) and `repository` (code).
# The free-form `note` field holds maintenance notes and is not shown (as in the CV).

status_labels <- c("ipa" = "in-principle accepted")

entry_status <- function(entry) {
  s <- trimws(gsub("[{}]", "", field(entry, "status")))
  if (!nzchar(s)) return("")
  lbl <- status_labels[tolower(s)]
  if (!is.na(lbl)) unname(lbl) else s
}

# Not yet published = has a status other than "in press"; these go under
# "Work in progress" (same routing as the CV built from the same bib).
is_wip <- function(entry) {
  s <- tolower(entry_status(entry))
  nzchar(s) && s != "in press"
}

# Published = no status, and a journal article, chapter, proceedings paper or
# book (misc/unpublished entries without status are preprints, software, ...)
is_published <- function(entry) {
  type <- tolower(attr(unclass(entry)[[1]], "bibtype"))
  !nzchar(entry_status(entry)) && !(type %in% c("misc", "unpublished"))
}

# "Registered report" label for published registered reports, linked to the
# registered report document from the bib (preferring Stage 1), e.g.
#   document = {stage 1 registered report: https://osf.io/xxxxx; stage 2 registered report}
rr_tag <- function(entry) {
  if (!is_published(entry)) return("")
  docs <- parse_documents(entry)
  rr <- docs[docs$kind == "rr", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rr) == 0) return("")
  rr <- rr[nzchar(rr$url), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rr) == 0) return('<span class="ref-tag">Registered report</span>')
  rr <- rr[order(!grepl("stage 1", tolower(rr$label))), , drop = FALSE]
  sprintf('<a class="ref-tag" href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="%s">Registered report</a>',
          rr$url[1], tools::toTitleCase(rr$label[1]))
}

# Parse the document field into a data frame of (label, url, kind)
doc_kind <- function(label) {
  l <- tolower(label)
  if (grepl("registered report", l)) "rr"
  else if (grepl("prereg", l)) "prereg"
  else if (grepl("preprint", l)) "preprint"
  else "other"
}

parse_documents <- function(entry) {
  d <- gsub("[{}]", "", field(entry, "document"))
  if (!nzchar(d)) return(data.frame(label = character(0), url = character(0), kind = character(0)))
  parts <- trimws(strsplit(d, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
  has_url <- grepl("^.*?:\\s*https?://", parts, perl = TRUE)
  label <- ifelse(has_url, trimws(sub("^(.*?):\\s*https?://.*$", "\\1", parts, perl = TRUE)), parts)
  url   <- ifelse(has_url, trimws(sub("^.*?:\\s*(https?://.*)$", "\\1", parts, perl = TRUE)), "")
  data.frame(label = label, url = url,
             kind = vapply(label, doc_kind, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Preprint servers' DOI prefixes (PsyArXiv, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv,
# Preprints.org, arXiv) and preprint URL patterns
preprint_doi_re <- "^10\\.(31234|31219|31235|31222|20944|48550)/"
preprint_url_re <- "osf\\.io/preprints/|psyarxiv\\.com|arxiv\\.org|preprints\\.org|doi\\.org/10\\.(31234|31219|31235|31222|20944|48550)/"

# Icon + label for each kind of link
link_style <- list(
  doi      = c("ai ai-doi",               "DOI"),
  preprint = c("bi bi-file-earmark-text", "Preprint"),
  prereg   = c("ai ai-preregistered",     "Preregistration"),
  rr       = c("ai ai-preregistered",     "Registered report"),
  osf      = c("ai ai-osf",               "OSF (materials, data)"),
  github   = c("bi bi-github",            "Code on GitHub"),
  code     = c("bi bi-code-slash",        "Code repository"),
  link     = c("bi bi-link-45deg",        "Link")
)

# Normalise a URL for duplicate detection
norm_url <- function(u) {
  u <- tolower(utils::URLdecode(trimws(u)))
  u <- sub("^http://", "https://", u)
  u <- sub("^https://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/", "https://doi.org/", u)
  sub("/+$", "", u)
}

make_links <- function(entry) {
  links <- list()   # each: c(url, kind, label)
  add <- function(url, kind, label = NULL) {
    if (!nzchar(url)) return(invisible())
    if (is.null(label)) label <- link_style[[kind]][2]
    links[[length(links) + 1]] <<- c(url, kind, label)
  }

  docs <- parse_documents(entry)
  # Document types listed without a URL describe the entry itself, so the entry's
  # own preprint-server DOI/URL is that document (e.g. a Stage 1 registered report)
  own_doc <- docs[!nzchar(docs$url) & docs$kind != "other", , drop = FALSE]
  own_kind  <- if (nrow(own_doc) > 0) own_doc$kind[1] else "preprint"
  own_label <- if (nrow(own_doc) > 0 && own_kind == "rr") tools::toTitleCase(own_doc$label[1]) else NULL

  classify_url <- function(url) {
    if (grepl("doi\\.org/10\\.17605/osf\\.io", url, ignore.case = TRUE)) return("osf")
    if (grepl(preprint_url_re, url, ignore.case = TRUE)) return("own")
    if (grepl("doi\\.org/", url, ignore.case = TRUE)) return("doi")
    if (grepl("osf\\.io", url, ignore.case = TRUE)) return("osf")
    if (grepl("github\\.com", url, ignore.case = TRUE)) return("github")
    "link"
  }
  add_classified <- function(url) {
    k <- classify_url(url)
    if (k == "own") add(url, own_kind, own_label) else add(url, k)
  }

  doi <- sub("^https?://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/", "", field(entry, "doi"))
  if (nzchar(doi)) add_classified(paste0("https://doi.org/", doi))

  url <- field(entry, "url")
  if (nzchar(url)) add_classified(url)

  # Published papers (no status, in a journal/book/proceedings) don't link their
  # preprint; preprint-only entries (misc/unpublished) still do, as the preprint
  # is the work itself
  published <- is_published(entry)

  # Linked documents: preprints, preregistrations, registered reports, ...
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(docs))) {
    if (!nzchar(docs$url[i])) next
    if (published && docs$kind[i] == "preprint") next
    # ... and carry their registered-report link on the "Registered report" label
    if (published && docs$kind[i] == "rr") next
    k <- if (docs$kind[i] == "other") "link" else docs$kind[i]
    lbl <- if (k %in% c("rr", "link")) tools::toTitleCase(docs$label[i]) else NULL
    add(docs$url[i], k, lbl)
  }

  osf <- field(entry, "osf")
  if (nzchar(osf)) add(osf, "osf")

  repo <- field(entry, "repository")
  if (nzchar(repo)) add(repo, if (grepl("github\\.com", repo, ignore.case = TRUE)) "github" else "code")

  # Drop links pointing at the same target (e.g. url just resolving the doi)
  icons <- c()
  seen <- c()
  for (l in links) {
    key <- norm_url(l[1])
    if (key %in% seen) next
    seen <- c(seen, key)
    icons <- c(icons, icon_link(l[1], link_style[[l[2]]][1], l[3]))
  }

  # Only offer a "find this on Google Scholar" link when the entry is actually
  # listed on Ingmar's Scholar profile (see on_scholar() / data/scholar-titles.txt) --
  # otherwise the search would turn up nothing useful and the icon would mislead.
  title <- gsub("[{}]", "", field(entry, "title"))
  if (nzchar(title) && on_scholar(title)) {
    scholar_url <- paste0("https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=", utils::URLencode(title, reserved = TRUE))
    icons <- c(icons, icon_link(scholar_url, "ai ai-google-scholar", "View on Google Scholar"))
  }

  if (length(icons) == 0) return("")
  paste0('<span class="ref-links">', paste(icons, collapse = ""), "</span>")
}

# Format a single author in APA style: "Family, F. M.", bolding Visser
format_person_apa <- function(p) {
  family <- paste(p$family, collapse = " ")
  given  <- p$given
  initials <- if (!is.null(given) && length(given) > 0 && any(nzchar(given))) {
    paste(sapply(given[nzchar(given)], function(g) paste0(substr(trimws(g), 1, 1), ".")), collapse = " ")
  } else ""
  name <- if (nzchar(initials)) paste0(family, ", ", initials) else family
  if (grepl("Visser", family, ignore.case = TRUE)) paste0("**", name, "**") else name
}

# Format authors APA-style, always listing every named author (no et-al truncation
# of our own; "et al." only appears when the bib entry itself has "and others")
format_authors <- function(entry) {
  e <- unclass(entry)[[1]]
  persons <- e[["author"]]
  if (is.null(persons) || length(persons) == 0) return("")

  n <- length(persons)
  last_is_others <- tolower(paste(persons[[n]]$family, collapse = " ")) == "others"
  names_fmt <- vapply(persons, format_person_apa, character(1))

  if (last_is_others) {
    if (n == 1) return("et al.")
    paste0(paste(names_fmt[-n], collapse = ", "), ", et al.")
  } else if (n == 1) {
    names_fmt
  } else if (n == 2) {
    paste(names_fmt[1], "&", names_fmt[2])
  } else {
    paste0(paste(names_fmt[-n], collapse = ", "), ", & ", names_fmt[n])
  }
}

# Format a single entry as a markdown list item
format_entry <- function(entry) {
  authors <- format_authors(entry)
  year    <- field(entry, "year")
  status  <- entry_status(entry)
  title   <- gsub("[{}]", "", field(entry, "title"))
  journal <- field(entry, "journal")
  volume  <- field(entry, "volume")
  number  <- field(entry, "number")
  pages   <- field(entry, "pages")
  booktitle <- field(entry, "booktitle")
  type    <- tolower(attr(unclass(entry)[[1]], "bibtype"))
  links   <- make_links(entry)

  # Build venue string
  venue <- ""
  if (nzchar(journal)) {
    venue <- paste0("*", journal, "*")
    if (nzchar(volume)) venue <- paste0(venue, ", ", volume)
    if (nzchar(number)) venue <- paste0(venue, "(", number, ")")
    if (nzchar(pages))  venue <- paste0(venue, ", ", pages)
  } else if (nzchar(booktitle)) {
    venue <- paste0("*", booktitle, "*")
  } else if (type == "phdthesis") {
    venue <- paste(c("Doctoral dissertation", field(entry, "school")[nzchar(field(entry, "school"))]), collapse = ", ")
  } else if (type == "techreport") {
    venue <- paste(c("Technical report", field(entry, "institution")[nzchar(field(entry, "institution"))]), collapse = ", ")
  } else {
    # No venue (preprints, registered reports, ...): describe the document type
    docs <- parse_documents(entry)
    if (nrow(docs) > 0) venue <- paste(tools::toTitleCase(unique(docs$label)), collapse = "; ")
  }
  venue <- sub("^(\\w)", "\\U\\1", venue, perl = TRUE)

  # Year, followed by the project status for not-yet-published work: "(2026, under review)"
  date <- paste(c(year, status)[nzchar(c(year, status))], collapse = ", ")

  line <- paste0("- ", authors)
  if (nzchar(date)) line <- paste0(line, " (", date, ")")
  line <- paste0(line, '. <span class="paper-title">', title, "</span>")
  if (nzchar(venue)) line <- paste0(line, ". ", venue)
  tag <- rr_tag(entry)
  if (nzchar(tag)) line <- paste0(line, " ", tag)
  if (nzchar(links)) line <- paste0(line, " ", links)
  line <- paste0(line, ".")

  line
}

# Read bib file
bib_main <- suppressMessages(ReadBib("ingmar.bib", check = "warn"))

entry_type <- function(b, i) tolower(attr(unclass(b[i])[[1]], "bibtype"))

# Separate work in progress (status set, other than "in press") from published
# work (no status, or in press)
wip_flags <- sapply(seq_along(bib_main), function(i) is_wip(bib_main[i]))

all_wip  <- bib_main[wip_flags]
pub_main <- bib_main[!wip_flags]

# Get year from entry
get_year <- function(entry) {
  y <- field(entry, "year")
  suppressWarnings(as.integer(y))
}
```

### Work in progress

::: {.refs-compact}

```{r results='asis'}
years_wip <- sapply(seq_along(all_wip), function(i) get_year(all_wip[i]))
ord <- order(is.na(years_wip), -ifelse(is.na(years_wip), 0L, years_wip))

for (i in ord) {
  cat(format_entry(all_wip[i]), "\n")
}
```

:::

### Journal articles

::: {.refs-compact}

```{r results='asis'}
pub_articles <- pub_main[sapply(seq_along(pub_main), function(i) entry_type(pub_main, i) == "article")]
years_art <- sapply(seq_along(pub_articles), function(i) get_year(pub_articles[i]))
unique_years <- sort(unique(years_art[!is.na(years_art)]), decreasing = TRUE)

for (yr in unique_years) {
  cat(sprintf("\n#### %d\n\n", yr))
  idx <- which(years_art == yr)
  titles_yr <- sapply(idx, function(i) field(pub_articles[i], "title"))
  idx <- idx[order(titles_yr)]
  for (i in idx) {
    cat(format_entry(pub_articles[i]), "\n")
  }
}
```

:::

    cat(format_entry(chapters[i]), "\n")

}
